chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Why the big band folded
summary: Rock dominated and he lacked money and an agency.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: I guess that takes us into the late Sixties and into the Seventies.
Well, we should be around '64 or somewhere around there. Because after the band got started, we did a lot of gigs. We played for the Mayor a couple of times.

Yeah. But there was not enough continuity to keep it going. But it was nice having a big band, you know, hearing all of them pretty sounds coming out of them beautiful changes. And we had several guys writing for the band, but we just couldn't hold it together.
Well, that was a period when Rock was really at its most popular....
...and Jazz was struggling against that even if you had a small group. And to keep a big band together was virtually impossible.

Yeah. Well, I don't say, you know, that I was the man that should have had the big band in the first place, because I didn't really have the money to be financing a big band, and I didn't have no agency that would do it either. And when you try to do it on your own, it's kind of rough.
You need somebody behind you with a venture like that.
Yeah. You need to have some money behind you anyway.
